title: Turning Tide
briefing: Kestrel Air has been flying high, but the weather can change. Remember that cash is a position too.
objective: Bull and bear markets. When prices keep falling and you can only buy, cash keeps you safe.
debrief: Kestrel Air rose for the first 13 days. On day 13 fuel prices jumped, the Harbor 50 slid, and the airline gapped down and kept falling in a bear phase. HODL Hannah never sells, so she rode it all the way down. Players who stepped into cash soon after the turn kept most of their early gains; waiting in cash at $0 beat losing money.

news.headline: Harbor 50 slides as fuel prices jump
news.body: Fuel prices rose sharply overnight. The Harbor 50 index fell, led by airlines, whose biggest cost is fuel.

basic.text: Be out of Kestrel Air (in cash) by day 20
